title: First patients enrolled in record-breaking Ebola treatment trial in DRC | Global health | The Guardian
snippet:
The Partners treatment trial has opened with two drugs on its books – remdesivir, and MBP134. Patients will be randomly allocated to receive either drug, a combination of the two, or simply standard, supportive care.

Remdesivir is an antiviral made by pharma company Gilead Sciences, while MBP134 is a monoclonal antibody developed by Mapp Biopharmaceutical, containing two specially engineered immune proteins that recognise and neutralise the virus. [...] Both are given intravenously – MBP134 as a one-off infusion, and remdesivir as 10 days of intravenous therapy.

“These two drugs actually have been proven to work against the Bundibugyo virus in animal models,” said Prof Laurens Liesenborghs of the Institute of Tropical Medicine, Antwerp, who is working on the trial in Ituri.

“They showed great efficacy, but now we need to test it in humans. Basically, what we want to see is if they indeed can lower mortality.” [...] WHO officials said enough remdesivir and MBP134 had been donated, by Gilead and the US government respectively, for 1,200 patients to be enrolled. The WHO is in discussions to ensure sufficient supplies will be available after the trial, should they prove safe and effective, it said.

Patients of any age, including pregnant and breastfeeding women, who are often excluded from medical research, can enrol in the trial.

title: Moderna's mRNA Ebola Vaccine Enters Human Trials: Platform Speed Meets Cold-Chain Wall in Ituri
snippet: Both vaccines target the same antigen — Bundibugyo's glycoprotein — but use fundamentally different delivery mechanisms. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV uses a chimpanzee adenovirus vector: a modified, replication-incompetent chimpanzee virus (its E1 gene deleted so it cannot propagate) that carries the glycoprotein gene as a DNA payload. Once inside the cell, the DNA is transcribed into mRNA and then translated into the glycoprotein. Using a chimpanzee-derived virus sidesteps a common problem with human [...] and builds immunological memory specific to Bundibugyo. The mRNA itself degrades within days and does not integrate into the cell's DNA. If the vaccinated person later encounters the virus, their immune system can respond rapidly. For a detailed review of the LNP delivery mechanism, see this PMC academic review. [...] Both vaccines target the same Bundibugyo glycoprotein, but via different mechanisms. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV uses a modified chimpanzee adenovirus to deliver a DNA copy of the glycoprotein gene into cells; the cell then transcribes that DNA into mRNA and produces the antigen. Moderna's mRNA-1469 delivers the mRNA directly, skipping the DNA step entirely. The mRNA platform offers faster development speed and manufacturing scalability; the adenoviral vector platform offers superior cold-chain

# WHO calls for Phase III Ervebo vaccine trial amid Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak

In the absence of a vaccine candidate for the Bundibugyo, panellists agreed to investigate Ervebo against the strain.

Abigail Beaney August 10, 2026

Share

 Copy Link
 Share on X
 Share on Linkedin
 Share on Facebook [...] Earlier in August, Moderna initiated a Phase I trial of its mRNA Ebola vaccine for the Bundibugyo variant. The first-in-human Phase I trial (NCT07737717), which will test Moderna’s vaccine candidate, mRNA-1469, has been approved by Health Canada. The study will take place at three sites in Canada and evaluate the safety, tolerability and immunogenicity of the mRNA vaccine in healthy adult participants. The study is expected to enrol approximately 80 participants. [...] The WHO held a vaccine committee meeting to discuss investigating Ervebo in the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. Credit: Michael Derrer Fuchs / Shutterstock.com

A panel held by the World Health Organization (WHO) has called for a Phase III trial of the Zaire Ebolavirus vaccine Ervebo to be investigated against the current Bundibugyo strain.
